topic_title: Systematic Study and Design of Agent Harnesses
topic_summary: Recent research across web and Hugging Face signals examines how agent harness design—focusing on context management, skill management, and component interaction—shapes the performance of self-evolving, long-horizon AI agents. These studies matter to ML practitioners because optimizing harness architectures directly improves agent robustness, computational efficiency, and compositional generalization across domains like scientific research, gameplay, and robotics.
topic_key_facts: [Webpage] Researchers systematically study harness design for self-evolving autoresearch agents along two dimensions: context management and skill management.
[Webpage] MatHarness couples execution robustness through pre-flight verification, expert-distilled skills, and just-in-time auditing for open-ended computational materials research.
[Webpage] AutoPILOT is a visual agent harness that allows a multimodal model to send a primitive action, start an open-loop macro, or write a closed-loop controller in each model call.
[Hugging Face] Embo-Harness investigates four components of the robotic agentic loop: prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, distilling six empirical findings.

topic_title: Advances in On-Policy Distillation for Language Models
topic_summary: Recent research papers introduce novel variants of on-policy distillation (OPD) to improve large language model post-training and agent efficiency. These methods include Contrastive On-Policy Distillation (cOPD) with dual-branch supervision, Muted Distillation (MD) to prevent reasoning length inflation, and Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation (CSPD) for continual RL expert consolidation.
topic_key_facts: cOPD provides dual branch supervision by contrasting strong teacher, weak teacher, and student predictions at student generated prefixes. [Webpage]
A controlled token intervention study suggests that even a model weaker than the student can serve as an informative contrastive reference. [Webpage]
Muted Distillation (MD) is a variant of OPD that hides the student's reasoning from the teacher so the teacher judges what the student does without interference. [Webpage]
CSPD keeps the pre-RL model frozen and distills each RL expert independently into a soft prompt. [Hugging Face]
CSPD composes experts by concatenating their prompts without joint training. [Hugging Face]

topic_title: Advances in Long-Video Understanding and Memory Systems for AI Agents
topic_summary: Recent research papers introduce new frameworks—including VideoGym, VTree, ORDO, and MORSE—to address core challenges in long-video understanding, agentic memory, and motion analysis for video LLMs. These developments matter to AI/ML practitioners because they tackle critical bottlenecks like sparse evidence retrieval, fixed-distribution reinforcement learning limitations, and bounded frame storage in streaming systems.
topic_key_facts: [Webpage] Text-heavy questions account for 58% of samples in the VideoGym source pool, compared to 15% graph-heavy, 17% visual-heavy, and 10% time-range questions.
[Webpage] VideoGym is presented as an adaptive reinforcement learning environment for long-video agents to locate sparse evidence.
[Webpage] VTree addresses hierarchical memory growth for agentic long-video understanding where standard uniform frame sampling discards fine-grained evidence.
[Webpage] ORDO is a proposed framework for fine-grained motion understanding in video large language models via order-dependent supervision.
[Hugging Face] MORSE stands for Memory Optimization with Recursive Self-Evolvement, an open-world auto-research method optimizing streaming memory design.

topic_title: Mitigating Positional and Permutation Biases in Large Models
topic_summary: Recent research papers introduce novel methods to address positional and permutation biases in multimodal and language models. These techniques—such as shared positions, attention-only distillation, and Exchangeable Self-Distillation—help models overcome issues like the lost-in-the-middle curve and permutation sensitivity without requiring gold answers.
topic_key_facts: [Webpage] The paper on reducing permutation sensitivity categorizes permutation bias phenomena into four representative scenarios. [Webpage]
[Webpage] Exchangeable Self-Distillation (ExSD) trains a small adapter on shuffled contexts to reproduce a model's answer when reading the answer document alone. [Webpage]
[Webpage] ExSD requires no gold answers and only a few thousand examples, tested across six models starting from size 1.5. [Webpage]
[Hugging Face] The DiLE framework combines task guidance with on-policy retrieval feedback to preserve discriminative evidence in universal multimodal embeddings. [Hugging Face]
